parts.title: Campsites
parts.transcript: S1: two friends choose a campsite. Westerly Campsite - for under-12s; located by the sea (1); special attraction = the animals children can feed (2); a local farmer sells eggs (3); campers allowed to make/have a fire (4); family of four costs 15.75 per night (5). Snetton Forest - recommended for people who like fishing (6); can hire a bike (7); organised football (8) for children. Trent Valley - better in July (9) for families (quieter than the June festival); has an outdoor pool (10).

questions.text: What is the most important attitude towards making mistakes according to Arthur?

options.text: Mistakes can be a chance to learn.

options.text: Try to get advice from books.

options.text: create products better than the competitors'

options.text: good business advice with new ideas

parts.transcript: S2: businessman Arthur Jones on starting a business. Mistakes show where to improve - a chance to learn (11=B). Self-confidence can make you ignore problems and even cause failure (12=A; gained through hard work not reading). Stay committed to your goal rather than aimlessly trying new things - keep their aims (13=C). For a marketing problem he found an expert - seek help from experts (14=B). Leaders should win the respect of their employees (15=C). Deal with risks with caution/carefully (16=A). Factors when starting a business: be committed + pay attention to detail (17/18=C,D; prices can't be fixed, can't guarantee better than competitors, strategy not a problem). Support that mattered: family (financial+mental) + bank loan (19/20=A,C; advice/ideas not practical, friends/government not cited).
parts.instruction: You will hear a radio programme about starting a business, presented by a businessman called Arthur Jones.

parts.transcript: S3: Mark and Fran prepare a presentation on NZ dolphins. Sounds focused through the 'melon' organ that most sea mammals lack - unusual anatomy of the head (21=B). Hector's dolphins unaffected by tourist numbers (not a problem yet) but harmed by gill nets and slow reproduction (22=A). The sanctuary was a consequence of a study by marine biologists - scientific research (23=B; public were supportive, fishing industry against). Biggest Hector's group off the West Coast (24=C; 89 off Southland, ~2000 East Coast). Matching: Common dolphins = whole NZ coast (25=C); Dusky = pods up to 800, large groups (26=B); Hector's = go in the wake/behind boats (27=A); Maui's = only western coastal waters off North Island = NW coast (28=F); Orcas = seen mostly in Kaikoura though they roam (29=H); Bottlenose = bigger than others but smaller than orca = second largest (30=G).
parts.instruction: You will hear a discussion between two students called Mark and Fran about their presentation on some dolphins which are unique to New Zealand.

parts.transcript: S4: Managing Director of Molectra Technologies on tyre recycling. 1.5 million tyres dumped in Australia per month (31). Old methods failed: burning made toxic fumes; companies made no profit (32). Molectra's process: smaller cheaper machines, tyres softened before shredding, costs cut 30%, and no limit on the size (33) of tyre handled. Plans to spend 5% of income on research (34). Process/uses: removal of steel wires (35) from the rim (-> steel pellets); chemicals remove dirt (36) and soften rubber; fibres (nylon/rayon) removed -> concrete reinforcement / sheets made of plastic (37) panels; crumb rubber -> asphalt, insulation, floor (38) tiles; Molectravac microwaves rubber to hydrocarbon -> activated carbon for water (39) treatment & air filtration; carbon black for batteries & ink (40); oil for electricity.
